subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should this be solved as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated authority marker now, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design in #71712?
rationale: The code change would define who may create or preserve host-elevated authority across persisted cron jobs and autonomous heartbeat runs, which is a security and product boundary rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Make #71712 the design owner, but explicitly include heartbeat elevated authority and last-modified provenance in that scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Provenance
options.body: Add the minimal per-job and heartbeat authority metadata now, with migration and tests for create/update/execute behavior.

options.title: Fail Closed First
options.body: Disable elevated execution for internal cron/heartbeat senders by default until a provenance model is approved, accepting upgrade disruption.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Make #71712 the design owner, but explicitly include heartbeat elevated authority and last-modified provenance in that scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the merged agent cron caller-scope boundary that this issue builds on.
